authorization: User requested investigating which datasets drive the remaining Kprime discrepancy before further author contact.
scope: Dataset influence, not rejection of experimental data, recovery of author selections, significance testing or development of a replacement EOS.
specimen_treatment: as_plotted in all cases; all prior estimated errors fixed at baseline
grouping: The three printed-error and nineteen estimated-error Isaak GGD KS rows form one 22-row series. Isaak GR-2B expansion remains a distinct specimen/series. Milani compression and thermal expansion are separate series. Two combined-publication deletions overlap the single-series deletions and must not be added.
fit_protocol: Same BM3, q-compromise thermal pressure, fixed Vm0=125.35 cm3/mol, Tr=298 K, n=20 and float32 R as preceding diagnostics. Same effective-variance IRLS protocol, tolerances and bounds. Two unchanged starts. Remove unused Kono/Gwanmesia scale parameters when their entire series is omitted; remap remaining scale indices without changing observations. In each published-Kprime profile, fix Kprime and optimize the other five parameters.
compute_cap: Exactly 32 declared scientific cases (baseline, fixed published Kprime, 12 disjoint-series deletions and 2 combined-publication deletions, under each of 2 normalizations), two starts each. Maximum 30 IRLS iterations, 400 evaluations per inner solve. Verification may replay declared cases; no post-result subset search.
score_protocol: At each constrained-Kprime solution, freeze its effective pressure errors. Evaluate original published six coefficients including published scales, freely fitted baseline coefficients, and constrained-Kprime fit on identical rows/errors. Sum standardized squared residuals by group. Residualize the Kprime derivative against the five nuisance columns over all rows. Group squared residualized derivatives partition conditional local information; minus residualized derivative times constrained residual divided by total information gives a signed local upward-Kprime contribution. Positive means upward pressure on Kprime in this linearized frozen-error diagnostic. This is not a nonlinear deletion effect or causal/likelihood attribution.
reporting: All rows, both starts, covariance, rank, bounds, convergence, source/baseline distances, signed deletion shifts and local group diagnostics. Do not rank merely by raw residual RMS or row count. Compare robust directions across the two fixed normalizations. Omitted-data fits can be unstable or lose identifiability; report rather than tuning.
preservation: Preserve canonical observations, errors, calibration, old plans/fits/manifests and published coefficients. No catalog changes or author contact. All diagnostic predictions remain not recommended.
